title: Primary Function of the System
learningObjectives: Connect suspension hardware to pushrod force transfer.
student: State the structural function of the pushrod within the pushrod-actuated suspension.
instructor: The pushrod transfers force and motion from the wheel-side suspension to the inboard rocker, which redirects motion to the spring-damper.

title: External Loads
learningObjectives: Identify the assigned critical pushrod load.
student: Identify the load transmitted through the pushrod and state whether the assigned critical load places the member in tension or compression.
instructor: The selected obstacle load case places the pushrod in axial compression. The assigned maximum force acts along the member's axis.

title: Supports and Boundary Conditions
learningObjectives: Relate rod ends to the pin-ended model.
student: Describe how spherical rod-end or pin connections motivate an idealized pinned-pinned column model.
instructor: Rod ends permit relative rotation and transmit force primarily through their centers, motivating an idealized pin at each end and K = 1.0.

title: Load Path
student: Trace the load path from the wheel-side suspension assembly through the pushrod to the rocker and spring-damper.
instructor: Road and wheel-side suspension demand passes through the upright and suspension links into the pushrod, then to the rocker and finally to the spring-damper and chassis attachments.

title: Critical Component or Location
student: Explain why the long, thin pushrod is a candidate for instability even when its average compressive stress is below yield.
instructor: A slender compression member can lose lateral stability at an Euler load below the load required to cause uniform material yielding.

title: Relevant Mechanical Response
student: Rank direct yielding and elastic buckling as possible responses and state what calculations are required to determine which governs.
instructor: Both must be evaluated. Compare the yield factor of safety from average compression with the Euler buckling factor of safety; the smaller nominal margin governs the simplified model.

title: Relevant Parameters
student: Identify the load, tube geometry, member length, elastic modulus, yield strength, and effective-length factor needed for the analysis.
instructor: The inputs are P, Do, t, L, E, Sy, and K. The inner diameter is derived rather than independently assigned.

title: Student-Generated Structural Idealization
student: Convert the highlighted pushrod into a straight hollow circular two-force member with pin-connected ends. Show equal and opposite compressive end forces, member length, and cross section.
instructor: A complete idealization shows a straight prismatic hollow tube, collinear equal and opposite compressive forces, pinned ends, length L, and circular annular cross section.

title: Modeling Assumptions
student: State the assumptions used to obtain the simplified axial-column model.
instructor: Assume central axial loading, pin-ended restraint, an initially straight prismatic member, constant hollow circular section, linear elasticity, and small deformation before buckling. Neglect crookedness, eccentricity, joint compliance, thread and insert stresses, bolt bending, weld effects, fatigue, impact amplification, and contact nonlinearities.

title: Mechanics Analysis Plan
learningObjectives: Plan the strength and stability checks.
student: Outline the calculation sequence before numerical work.
instructor: Determine Di, A, I, and r; calculate average compressive stress and yield factor of safety; calculate KL/r, Euler critical load, and buckling factor of safety; compare the two margins; then assess adequacy and limitations.

title: Boundary Conditions
learningObjectives: State the pin-ended idealization and K.
student: Identify the idealized end conditions and effective-length factor K.
instructor: The assigned model is pinned-pinned with K = {{pushrod_K}}.

title: Internal Axial Load
student: For the critical obstacle load case, determine the internal axial force N and state whether it is tension or compression.
instructor: N = {{pushrod_N_N}} N in compression.

title: Cross-Section Properties
student: Calculate Di, A, I, and radius of gyration r for the hollow circular tube.
instructor: Di = {{pushrod_Di_mm}} mm, A = {{pushrod_A_mm2}} mm2, I = {{pushrod_I_mm4}} mm4, and r = {{pushrod_r_mm}} mm.

title: Direct Compressive Stress
student: Calculate the average direct compressive stress sigma = P/A.
instructor: sigma = {{pushrod_sigma_MPa}} MPa in compression.

title: Yielding Factor of Safety
student: Using the assigned yield strength, calculate ny = Sy/sigma.
instructor: ny = {{pushrod_ny}}.

title: Slenderness Evaluation
student: Calculate KL/r using consistent units and explain why member length and radius of gyration affect buckling susceptibility.
instructor: KL/r = {{pushrod_slenderness}}. Greater effective length increases susceptibility, while a larger radius of gyration reduces it.

title: Euler Buckling Load
student: Calculate Pcr = pi2EI/(KL)2.
instructor: Pcr = {{pushrod_Pcr_kN}} kN.

title: Buckling Factor of Safety
student: Calculate nb = Pcr/P.
instructor: nb = {{pushrod_nb}}.

title: Governing Response
student: Compare ny and nb. Which mode provides the smaller nominal margin, and do both assigned checks pass?
instructor: The governing nominal response is {{pushrod_governing_mode}}, with governing ratio {{pushrod_governing_ratio}}. {{pushrod_assessment}}

title: Sensitivity and Design Modification
learningObjectives: Relate design variables to nominal capacity.
student: Explain how larger tube diameter, larger wall thickness, shorter unsupported length, larger E, or altered end restraint affect Euler capacity. Recommend a change appropriate to the governing response.
instructor: {{pushrod_sensitivity_assessment}}

title: Engineering Assessment and Recommendation
student: State whether the baseline pushrod passes the two nominal checks, identify the governing response, quote both safety factors, recommend one mechanics-based change if needed, and state at least one important limitation of the model.
instructor: {{pushrod_assessment}}
